stem: After an authorized emitter correction, what evidence best supports closure?
choices: Close the issue when the original alarm or deviation indicator is no longer present after the repair.
Repeat representative output or uniformity measurements under comparable conditions and confirm that the corrected system now meets the relevant performance expectation.
Close the issue when the technician and maintenance worker agree that the emitter repair appears successful.
Use short-term plant response as the main closure evidence because biological improvement is the intended outcome of the correction.
rationale: Repair closure should verify the performance condition that originally failed. Repeating representative output or uniformity measurements under comparable conditions provides direct before/after evidence that the irrigation system now performs as intended. An alarm state, subjective confidence, or immediate plant appearance may contribute context but does not independently prove that delivery uniformity was restored.
